scenario: LEXP.7.19: `==` on two whole `Json` values answers by [LFAC.2.5.1]'s deep structural equality. Pair p1 holds the same object in both slots with its members in a different order, so `p.a == p.b` is true and the rule fires; pair p2 differs in one leaf and does not fire. Two Pairs plus one Found. PATH PINNED: a slot-versus-slot test inside one pattern, which no alpha test can carry (there is no `Json` literal), so the predicate evaluator answers it: libds `rete/eval.c` `val_cmp` through the BINOP comparison arm; Mercury `ds.eval` `compare_outcome`. The differing member order is what pins structural rather than byte equality.
rules_ds:
schema Pair scope logical:
    id: String key
    a: Json mutable
    b: Json mutable

schema Found scope logical:
    id: String key

rule r:
    Pair p where p.a == p.b
->
    emit Found logical id: p.id
